title: Plan shift grace credits and auto-proration acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
background: Customers commonly change plans mid-billing-cycle (upgrades, downgrades, temporary bursts). Current behavior creates confusing invoice line items, inconsistent quota carry-forwards, and manual ops work to reconcile credits. We need a consistent policy that: (1) grants a short grace window for plan changes where credits or burst allowances are carried forward (snapback), (2) auto-prorates recurring fees and entitlements for the remainder of the billing period, and (3) produces clear invoice lines and usage attributions so customers and support can reconcile without manual adjustments.
description: This ticket defines acceptance criteria and edge-case handling for 'plan shift grace credits' and automatic proration logic. Scope covers hosted API customers on monthly plans and committed Dedicated customers where billing is managed by Redwood. The feature includes UI flags in the Console billing page, API endpoints for querying pending proration adjustments, and backend rules for computing credit amounts and invoice line items. We must account for token-based usage, per-route burst credits, reserved capacity reservations, and negative balance protections. This PRD is intentionally prescriptive to enable engineering to implement deterministic billing behavior and to reduce ops escalations.
scope: In scope: automatic calculation of prorated recurring fees when switching plans mid-cycle; short grace window (configurable, default 72 hours) where unused entitlements from the previous plan are credited in full or partially; rules for how burst credits are converted to monetary credits; producing an itemized proration preview in Console and via the billing API; invoice line items that surface: old-plan refund, new-plan charge, entitlement-credit, resulting balance and any immediate invoices or credits applied. Out of scope: one-off manual invoice adjustments by Billing Ops (handled by separate ops playbook); cross-currency rounding policy changes; marketplace/third-party reseller flows.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: When a customer upgrades a monthly plan during a billing period, the system must create a proration preview showing: old-plan refund amount, new-plan charge for remainder period, resulting net charge or credit, and a breakdown of entitlement changes (token quota, burst credits).

AC-2: When a customer downgrades, the system must either issue a monetary credit (if policy allows) or convert remaining entitlements into time-limited grace credits. The chosen policy must be applied consistently and be visible in the Console with the reason code 'plan-downgrade-proration'.

AC-3: Default grace window is 72 hours from plan change; within this window, previously purchased burst credits are eligible for conversion at a configurable conversion rate (default: 100% for unused burst credits, except where plan terms prohibit).

AC-4: For customers with reserved Dedicated capacity (monthly commit), plan changes do not auto-refund committed capacity fees; instead show a 'commitment adjustment' line and guidance to contact Sales. The UI must show a clear callout when a selected change affects committed capacity.

AC-5: All proration computations must be reproducible by engineers: the API must expose a /billing/proration-preview endpoint returning (as structured JSON) the computed values; the Console preview must match the API output within ±$0.01 after rounding. (QA verifies by calling both endpoints and comparing results.)

AC-6: Negative balance protection: if a downgrade would create a negative customer account balance, the system must either apply a post-pay authorization hold or require acceptance of a next-invoice charge; the behavior must be surfaced in the Console before the change is committed.

AC-7: Invoices created due to proration must include machine-readable metadata tags: original_subscription_id, change_timestamp, proration_policy_version. These tags must be included in the billing export CSV and be queryable in reports within 24 hours.

AC-8: Support and Billing Ops must be able to reproduce the proration calculation from the Console using a 'Recompute for support' workflow that includes the original timestamp and tenant id; this action logs a readonly audit entry.

AC-9: Edge case: if user consumed more tokens than new-plan quota before proration takes effect, overage should be calculated against the old plan until the plan change effective time; then quota resets according to new plan for subsequent requests. Acceptance verified via integration test injecting usage events around the change timestamp.

AC-10: Retroactive adjustments (e.g., refunds issued >30 days after change) must surface in the invoices as 'adjustment' lines and must not alter historical quota metrics used for auditing; acceptance verified by sample reconciliation report that matches the ledger entries.
decisions: D-1: Default grace window = 72 hours; configurable per-account via support request.
D-2: Unused burst credits convert to monetary credit at 100% by default for hosted monthly plans; Dedicated commitments excluded by default.
D-3: Proration preview is generated client-side by calling backend preview API; change is not applied until user confirms in Console or via confirm_proration API call.
open_questions: Q-1: Should proration previews include estimated tax, or should tax be computed only at final invoice time? (Finance input requested.)
Q-2: For multi-tenant orgs with pooled quotas, how should per-team plan changes affect pooled entitlements? (Needs policy decision.)
Q-3: Do we allow customers to opt into auto-apply credits immediately, or require manual acceptance in Console?
Q-4: What retention window should proration preview data have for audit (30/90/365 days)?
Q-5: For cross-currency accounts, which FX rate should be used for conversion of credits when plan change crosses billing currency?
notes: Implementation strategy: billing-service will compute monetary deltas; invoicing-service will create invoice adjustments. Console will call billing-service preview and show a side-by-side breakdown. A lightweight feature flag 'proration-v2' will gate rollout to 5% of orgs first.
QA plan: unit tests for boundary timestamps, integration tests that simulate usage events across change times, and end-to-end UX validation with sample customers.
Measurement: track support tickets referencing 'proration' and 'confusing invoice' and aim to reduce manual billing adjustments by 60% in Q2 after rollout.
